events.title: Last day of Steam Next Fest: two levels of Babylonian Twins free in the demo
events.summary: Steam Next Fest ends on Monday, October 26 at 10am PT, and Babylonian Twins is still part of it.The free demo includes the first two levels of the Royal Prison, including the Blazing Dungeon. Freeze one twin into a stone statue, use him as a step or a weight, and get the other one through.The game was made in Baghdad in 1993 for the Commodore Amiga. events.title: Next Fest replay: watch Babylonian Twins (recorded gameplay, not live)
events.summary: This is a recorded replay, not a live stream. It loops here on the store page until Steam Next Fest ends on Monday, October 26 at 10am PT.Babylonian Twins was made in Baghdad in 1993. The Definitive Edition brings it to Steam: two brothers, one puzzle-filled journey through ancient Babylon.The free demo is out now. If you enjoy it, please add Babylonian Twins to your wishlist.

events.title: The 1993 Amiga original: free today on itch, and built into the Steam version
events.summary: Thirty-three years ago I was an engineering student in Baghdad making a puzzle-platformer on an Amiga. It was finished, and it never shipped.As of today it's out, free. The original 1993 two-disk Amiga version of Babylonian Twins is on itch.io as it was: the levels, Mahir AlSalman's music, Murtadha Salman's pixel art. Boot it in FS-UAE, WinUAE, or on real hardware. events.title: Babylonian Twins — made in Baghdad, 1993. The Definitive Edition, 2026.
events.summary: Thirty-three years ago, in Baghdad, under sanctions, we made a video game on a Commodore Amiga — the first commercial video game ever made in Iraq. It never got its release. The masters survived on floppy disks that crossed borders in a backpack. Today, Babylonian Twins has a Steam page. Wishlist it, and you'll be there for the ending of a very long story.
